title: CiteGuard: Conformal False-Discovery Control for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
claim: A claim-level pipeline turns evidence scores into calibrated p-values, then applies multiple-testing control to keep only supported claims with guaranteed error rate.
layout: 5 colored panels, left-to-right, arrows between stages, legend strip below
description: A wide figure with five pastel-colored rounded panels read left to right, with a legend bar underneath. The first panel, Query & Retrieval, shows the query 'When was the Eiffel Tower built?', top-K passages, and a draft answer split into claims c1–c3, with the false claim c3 'Located in Tokyo' in red. Panel A (blue, offline) shows a stack of transformer blocks forming a cross-encoder scorer, a histogram of null scores, and a rank-based p-value formula. Panel B (orange) scores each claim, giving s1=0.94, s2=0.74 and s3=0.22, and places the resulting p-values on a number line. Panel C (purple) plots p-value against rank, with BH (blue) and BY (red) lines and a user-specified α. It lists which claims each procedure accepts or abstains on. The final green panel shows the faithful output with the unsupported claim withheld and a boxed guarantee, FDR ≤ α. The legend marks forward data flow, the calibration plug-in, kept claims and abstained claims.
caption: CITEGUARD pipeline. A draft answer for query q is decomposed into claims c1, c2, c3, each scored against retrieved evidence Ei
abstract: Large language models increasingly rely on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground responses in external corpora. Yet, even with strong retrievers, generated statements can remain unsupported, and the resulting citations are often not reliable indicators of evidence. We introduce CiteGuard, a RAG decoding layer that treats sentence-level factuality as a multiple-testing problem and combines conformal calibration with false-discovery-rate control. CiteGuard converts claim–evidence scores into p-values for the null hypothesis "unsupported" and uses BH/BY procedures to decide which claims to keep (with citations) and which to abstain on. On FEVER and Natural Questions, CiteGuard reduces the false-discovery rate among accepted claims from 28–31% (vanilla RAG) to below 10% at α=0.10, while retaining 86–92% of supported claims. This yields a user-controlled risk budget: practitioners can trade off faithfulness and coverage via α, with finite-sample guarantees under standard exchangeability assumptions.
